title: Kúnigseq Visits the Land of Shades
subtitle: A visitor must not eat the underworld berries

learningObjectives.text: What is the Land of Shades like?

visit.author: Greenlandic storytellers, collected by Knud Rasmussen
visit.excerpt: There was once a wizard whose name was Kúnigseq. One day, when he was about to call on his helping spirits and make a flight down into the underworld, he gave orders that the floor should be swilled with salt water, to take off the evil smell which might otherwise frighten his helping spirits away. Then he began to call upon his helping spirits, and without moving his body, began to pass downward through the floor. And down he went. On his way he came to a reef, which was covered with weed, and therefore so slippery that none could pass that way. And as he could not pass, his helping spirit lay down beside him, and by placing his foot upon the spirit, he was able to pass. And on he went, and came to a great slope covered with heather. Far down in the underworld, men say, the land is level, and the hills are small; there is sun down there, and the sky is also like that which we see from the earth. Suddenly he heard one crying: "Here comes Kúnigseq." By the side of a little river he saw some children looking for greyfish. And before he had reached the houses of men, he met his mother, who had gone out to gather berries. When he came up to her, she tried again and again to kiss him, but his helping spirit thrust her aside. "He is only here on a visit," said the spirit. Then she offered him some berries, and these he was about to put in his mouth, when the spirit said: "If you eat of them, you will never return.
visit.note: Verbatim English rendering by Worster from stories collected by Rasmussen in Greenland. The book title uses an outdated ethnonym; this lesson identifies the collection's Greenland scope.

narrativeBlocks.title: The shaman's descent
narrativeBlocks.body: Kúnigseq is the Greenland tale's journeyer — a man (or a shaman, in the telling) who makes the dangerous descent to the Land of Shades below.

narrativeBlocks.title: The passage down
narrativeBlocks.body: The way to the shades is through peril — narrow passages, beings that test him — the underworld is reached only by someone who knows the road or dares it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The land of the dead
narrativeBlocks.body: The shades live on below — a shadow-people in a world like and unlike ours: they have their dwellings, their routines, their own kind of life in the dark.

narrativeBlocks.title: What he learns there
narrativeBlocks.body: The journeyer watches the dead and returns with what the tale wants him to know: that the dead go on in their way, and the living must keep the customs that keep the two worlds apart.

narrativeBlocks.title: A Greenland underworld
narrativeBlocks.body: The Land of Shades is Greenland's own geography of the dead — different from a river-crossing or a nine-level descent: a whole society of shades beneath the living.

quiz.prompt: What is the Land of Shades?

choices.text: A frozen waste beyond the ice
The Greenland underworld — a whole society of the dead living their shadow-life below

quiz.explanation: The dead have their own world — parallel, dark, and populated.

quiz.prompt: What does the journey teach the living?

choices.text: That the dead go on in their way — and the living must keep the customs that keep the worlds apart
That the dead are angry and must be appeased
That the shaman can steal the shades' fire
That the dead forget the living entirely

quiz.explanation: The descent is a lesson in boundaries — the dead are other, and the customs hold the line.
